core: Climate as an enabling and constraining factor for settlement, agriculture, and population distribution
The settled science: the climate is warming and human greenhouse-gas emissions are the dominant cause (IPCC AR6, dated and attributed)
Human impacts geographers study: sea-level rise on coasts, agricultural and water shifts, extreme weather, climate-related displacement
Adaptation vs mitigation as the two categories of response
The distinction between settled science/measured impacts and contested, normative policy
supporting: Definitions: climate vs weather, greenhouse gas, anthropogenic, attribution
Precise language for displacement (internal displacement vs refugee)
Dated global figures for temperature, sea level, food-system emissions, and displacement
outOfScope: The general human-environment relationship and the determinism/possibilism debate (owned by environment-and-society)
Legal definitions of refugee/asylum-seeker/IDP and the 1951 Convention (owned by refugees-and-displacement)
Detailed treatment of agriculture and migration mechanics (owned by those topics)
Advocacy for any specific climate policy, carbon-pricing design, or emissions target

claims.claim: Climate, together with the uneven distribution of usable fresh water, shapes where people can live, farm, and build settlements, which is why world population is distributed unevenly.
The IPCC AR6 Working Group I report (2021) states it is unequivocal that human influence has warmed the atmosphere, ocean, and land.
Global surface temperature in 2011-2020 was about 1.1 degrees Celsius (1.09 C, range 0.95-1.20) higher than the 1850-1900 pre-industrial baseline.
NASA reported 2024 as the warmest year in its record (which begins in 1880), about 1.28 C above the 1951-1980 average and roughly 1.47 C above the 1850-1900 baseline.

Global mean sea level rose about 9.1 cm (3.6 in) since satellite altimetry began in 1993, with the rate of rise increasing from roughly 2.1 to 4.5 mm/yr, driven by thermal expansion and land-ice melt.
Food systems account for an estimated 21 to 37 percent of total net anthropogenic greenhouse-gas emissions (medium confidence).

About 45.8 million disaster-related internal displacements occurred in 2024, over 99 percent weather-related, contributing to a record of about 83 million people living in internal displacement worldwide at the end of 2024.

Climate responses divide into mitigation (reducing or removing greenhouse gases, addressing the cause) and adaptation (adjusting human systems to impacts, addressing the consequences); the two are complementary.

The basic physical science is settled and should not be framed as a debate, whereas specific policy choices (emissions pace, carbon pricing, targets, cost-sharing) are genuinely contested normative questions.

conflictingEvidence.issue: Reported displacement totals vary by count type (stock of IDPs at year end vs flow of new displacements in a year) and by cause (conflict vs disaster).
positions: IDMC GRID 2025: ~45.8 million new disaster-related internal displacements in 2024 (a flow), >99% weather-related
IDMC/IOM: ~83 million people living in internal displacement at end of 2024 (a stock, all causes including conflict)
conflictingEvidence.resolution: The lesson states both figures with their correct meaning (new disaster displacements vs total living in displacement) and attributes them to IDMC GRID 2025, avoiding conflation of flow and stock.

unsupportedExistingClaims: The generated draft was topic-agnostic boilerplate ('Climate And Society is a foundational concept...') that made no substantive climate claims; nothing in it was usable as evidence.

sourceRecords.title: Climate Change 2023: Synthesis Report (AR6), Summary for Policymakers
sourceRecords.notes: IPCC synthesis of AR6. Supports: human activities unequivocally caused ~1.1 C warming (2011-2020 vs 1850-1900); human influence dominant cause; mitigation vs adaptation framing as the two response categories. Reused verbatim from source-registry; also cross-checked headline against the WG1 SPM copy on ipcc.ch.

sourceRecords.title: 2025 Global Report on Internal Displacement (GRID 2025)
sourceRecords.notes: Authoritative humanitarian monitor of internal displacement. Supports: ~45.8 million disaster-related internal displacements in 2024, >99% weather-related; ~83 million people living in internal displacement at end of 2024 (a record). Figures obtained 2026-08-19 via WebSearch of GRID 2025 coverage and corroborated by IOM's release ('Record 83 Million People Living in Internal Displacement Worldwide'). Referenced for climate-linked displacement scale only; legal definitions are deferred to the refugees-and-displacement topic.
